mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) consistently compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% over a 3-month period, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which triggers a negative S&P 500 return over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 1% from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising above 2.0% and CPIAUCSL above 2.0% YoY), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and CPIAUCSL > 2.0% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market, indicated by a high payroll employment growth (PAYEMS > 100k monthly), consistently supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS growth exceeds 100k.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 (index base 2017=100), it signals a contraction in manufacturing and supply chain disruptions, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100.

mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) combined with high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.0% YoY) indicates an aggressive monetary policy response to inflation, which compresses equity valuations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is rising and CPIAUCSL > 2.0% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (as indicated by high GDP growth and strong consumer spending), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to valuation compression and the anticipation of monetary tightening, leading to negative returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth > 2.0% and RSAFS growth > 0.5%.
